name: Boiled Frosting
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: finest pulverized sugar
ingredients.originalText: one pound of finest pulverized sugar

ingredients.name: vanilla, rose-water, or lemon juice for seasoning
ingredients.originalText: vanilla, rose-water, or lemon juice for seasoning

instructions.text: Add three wine-glassfuls of clear water to one pound of finest pulverized sugar
Let it stand until it dissolves
Boil it until it is perfectly clear and threads from the spoon
Beat well the whites of four eggs
Pour the sugar into the dish with the eggs, but do not mix them until the syrup is luke-warm
Beat all well together for one-half hour
Season to your taste with vanilla, rose-water, or lemon juice
Rub the cake with a little flour before you apply the icing
Put the first coating on the cake as soon as it is well mixed
While the first coat is drying continue to beat the remainder
Set the cake in a warm place near the fire

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Add three wine-glassfuls of clear water to one pound of finest pulverized sugar
2. Let it stand until it dissolves
3. Boil it until it is perfectly clear and threads from the spoon
4. Beat well the whites of four eggs
5. Pour the sugar into the dish with the eggs, but do not mix them until the syrup is luke-warm
6. Beat all well together for one-half hour
7. Season to your taste with vanilla, rose-water, or lemon juice
8. Rub the cake with a little flour before you apply the icing
9. Put the first coating on the cake as soon as it is well mixed
10. While the first coat is drying continue to beat the remainder
11. Set the cake in a warm place near the fire
